widgets_values:
CUPID3D — ADVANCED SCENE INTEGRATION

Reconstructs the subject in 3D, puts it back into the photo it came from, and then has Klein 3 blend that render into the plate so it reads as a photograph rather than a paste-up.

NEEDS, BEYOND THIS PACK
- ComfyUI-NKD-Basic-Tools — NKD Loader, NKD Mask Picker
- ComfyUI-NKD-Klein-Tools — Klein Pre/Postsampling, Box Detections, Reference Control
- ComfyUI-NKD-VFX-Tools — NKD Preview 3D
- ComfyUI-NKD-Preview-Tools — Popup Preview
- ComfyUI-NKD-Notes — the hint pinned to Reference Control
- RES4LYF — ClownsharKSampler Beta
- basic_data_handling — IfElse
Models: a SAM checkpoint for the Mask Picker, and the "Klein 3 Distilled" bundle inside NKD Loader.

PICK THE SUBJECT FIRST
NKD Mask Picker is where this starts: click the subject in the image and it returns one mask, which does three jobs — it is the subject for Cupid3D, the region for the removal edit, and the box for the detections. Nothing else needs touching to change subject.

TWO KLEIN PASSES
1. REMOVE — the same mask drives a "remove the object" edit that clears the subject off the photo and leaves a clean plate. IfElse picks that plate or the untouched photo, and whatever it picks also sets the viewer's size through Get Image Size, so camera and plate cannot disagree.

2. BLEND — NKD Preview 3D renders the mesh over that plate through the predicted camera. Its render goes in as <Picture 1> and the untouched photo as <Picture 2>. The prompt is built by String Concatenate: describe the scene in the string node and the blend instruction is appended to it. Reference Control holds reference 1 — ref_1, the original photo — and its weight is the dial for how hard the blend pulls back towards the photo.

The result lands in Popup Preview with the original wired as its reference, so before and after sit side by side.

place_on_ground rests the mesh on y=0; crop_to_content is off here, so the pose is solved on the full frame.

widgets_values_named.text:
CUPID3D — one image in, a 3D mesh plus the camera that shot it.

First run downloads ~7 GB of weights from hbb1/Cupid, then takes a minute or so. Peak VRAM is about 11.5 GB.

WHY THE EXTRA NODES

- InvertMask: LoadImage's MASK is 1 - alpha, so it marks the background. Cupid3D wants the subject. Segmentation nodes (RMBG, SAM) already give the subject, so they wire straight in with no InvertMask. With no mask at all, rembg removes the background itself.

- GetImageSize -> RenderMesh width/height: Cupid predicts an off-centre principal point, and LOAD3D_CAMERA has no field for one, so the node pads the frame until that point is centred. 'camera_frame' is that padded frame, and it is what the camera describes. Render at its size and composite against it, not against the original image.

camera_info is a plain LOAD3D_CAMERA, so it also drives Preview3D, Load3D and the NKD VFX Tools camera nodes.

The mesh carries vertex colours, not a baked texture. For UVs and a texture, run it through UnwrapMesh and BakeTextureFromViews.
